finding.title: Hoist the child-list sort out of the per-curriculum loop in ContentTree.fromCurricula

evidence.quote:
// Sort each child list by sortOrder so display is stable.
      for (final list in childrenByContainerKey.values) {

finding.why: The sort block at lines 126-129 iterates `childrenByContainerKey.values` — the map accumulated across ALL curricula processed so far — but it sits inside the outer `for (final entry in byCurriculum.entries)` loop (opens line 93, the sort closes at line 130 still inside it). For 9 curricula this re-sorts every earlier curriculum's already-sorted child lists up to 9 times each instead of once. contentTree is a keepAlive provider built synchronously (no isolate offload) the first time any screen reads it, so this redundant O(9x) work sits directly on that first-access latency, not merely a style nit.
finding.recommendation: Move the sort block outside the curriculum loop (one dedent) so each child list is sorted exactly once after all curricula are indexed.
acceptance_criteria: The sort loop executes once, after the curriculum loop, in content_tree.dart.
Existing children()-ordering assertions in epic_25_schema_core_test.dart continue to pass.

finding.title: Route hierarchy_browser.dart's empty-state text through AppLocalizations instead of a hardcoded English literal
finding.rule: AX-2 — no hardcoded user-facing strings; EN/HE parity
finding.why: This is the default emptyBuilder used whenever the caller doesn't supply one. The sole current caller, HierarchySelectionPanel (hierarchy_selection_panel.dart:299), does not pass emptyBuilder, so this branch is live and reachable whenever path/scope filtering leaves zero items at a level (a real occurrence in the bulk-mark, lifetime-marking, and add-track-flow screens that embed this panel). A Hebrew-locale user who hits it sees raw English 'No content available' instead of the Hebrew translation — even though the exact ARB key needed (`contentHierarchyNoContent`) already exists and is used correctly one file over in content_hierarchy_screen.dart's own empty-state branch.
finding.recommendation: Replace the literal with `AppLocalizations.of(context)!.contentHierarchyNoContent` (already translated, already in the ARB catalog) or require callers to always pass an emptyBuilder.
acceptance_criteria: hierarchy_browser.dart's default empty state renders via AppLocalizations, not a string literal.
A Locale('he') widget test pumping HierarchySelectionPanel with a filtered-to-empty item set asserts the Hebrew string renders.

finding.title: Move hierarchy_selection_test.dart to its AG-5-mirrored path under test/core/content/

evidence.quote: // Tests for HierarchySelection — covers == and hashCode (lines 218-228).

finding.why: git log shows commit ee270013 ('extract ContentBrowserTree widget; move HierarchySelection to core') relocated the class from features/onboarding/domain/services/ into lib/core/content/hierarchy_selection.dart, but its test file was never moved — it still lives at the pre-move features/onboarding path, and its own header comment cites line numbers ('218-228') that haven't existed since the move. AG-5's stated purpose is exactly this: an agent globbing test/core/content/ for HierarchySelection's tests today finds nothing (only the unrelated coarse_unit_leaf_refs_test.dart), and could easily write a duplicate test file instead of finding/extending the real one.
finding.recommendation: git mv test/features/onboarding/domain/services/hierarchy_selection_test.dart to test/core/content/hierarchy_selection_test.dart and fix the stale header comment.
acceptance_criteria: hierarchy_selection_test.dart exists at test/core/content/hierarchy_selection_test.dart and nowhere else.
The pending AG-5 unmirrored-test audit check (once implemented) passes for this file.

finding.title: Consolidate the duplicate 0-indexed/1-indexed level-value accessors in content_grouping.dart

evidence.quote:
String? _levelValueAt(ContentItem item, int depth) => switch (depth) {
  0 => item.level1,

String? levelValueAt(ContentItem item, int level) => switch (level) {
  1 => item.level1,

finding.why: Two functions differing only by a leading underscore implement the identical level1..level4 switch, one 0-indexed (internal, used by groupItemsByNextLevel) and one 1-indexed (public, used by hierarchy_browser.dart and hierarchy_selection_panel.dart). The near-identical names with different index conventions is exactly the kind of thing a future edit touches in one copy and forgets in the other, or a caller picks the wrong one and is off by one level.
finding.recommendation: Keep only the public 1-indexed levelValueAt and have groupItemsByNextLevel call it with `depth + 1`, deleting the private 0-indexed twin.
acceptance_criteria: content_grouping.dart has one level-value accessor function, not two.
coarse_unit_leaf_refs_test.dart and existing grouping behavior are unchanged.

finding.title: Add direct unit/widget tests for content_grouping.dart's groupItemsByNextLevel and for HierarchyBrowser
finding.why: Repo-wide grep for groupItemsByNextLevel(, collapseAmudLeaf(, itemDisplayName(, levelValueAt(, and HierarchyBrowser( inside test/ finds zero direct references. content_grouping.dart's only test file, coarse_unit_leaf_refs_test.dart, covers 2 of its ~8 exported symbols and isn't even AG-5-named for this source (the mirrored name would be content_grouping_test.dart, which doesn't exist). HierarchyBrowser is exercised only transitively, three levels down, through unrelated parent-widget tests (bulk_mark_screen_test.dart, recent_activity_and_hierarchy_panel_l1_test.dart, r2_panel_leaf_crumb_ellipsis_test.dart) — never directly. This is the concrete reason the maxBrowseDepth dead-branch bug (separate finding) and content_tree.dart's parent() off-by-one (separate finding, in the sibling keepAlive-provider file which likewise has no direct unit test, only story-acceptance coverage) went unnoticed: the pure logic they live in has no focused unit test that would exercise the argument or the ordering that triggers them.
finding.recommendation: Add test/core/content/content_grouping_test.dart covering groupItemsByNextLevel (including the maxBrowseDepth branch), collapseAmudLeaf, itemDisplayName, and levelValueAt directly; add a HierarchyBrowser widget test independent of HierarchySelectionPanel.
acceptance_criteria: test/core/content/content_grouping_test.dart exists and unit-tests groupItemsByNextLevel directly, including a maxBrowseDepth case.
A widget test pumps HierarchyBrowser directly (drill-down, navigateBack, autoAdvanceSingleOption, empty state) without going through HierarchySelectionPanel.
